name: Global Trade & Agricultural Policy

objectives.text: Identify agricultural products grown in the United States that are sold to other countries
Identify foods and agricultural products the United States buys from other countries and explain why they are grown elsewhere
Describe how international trade allows countries to buy and sell agricultural products
Locate the major trading partners of the United States for agricultural products on a world map
Explain how differences in climate, soil, water, labor, and technology give countries an advantage in producing certain agricultural products
Describe the purpose of the Farm Bill and the major types of programs it funds, such as commodity support, conservation, crop insurance, and nutrition assistance
Explain how tariffs and trade agreements affect the price of agricultural products
Explain how agricultural trade affects food security in importing and exporting countries
Explain the importance of agricultural exports to the United States economy and to rural communities
Describe how agricultural policy is made, including the roles of Congress, the USDA, commodity groups, and producer organizations
Compare major trade agreements and institutions, such as USMCA and the World Trade Organization, and the rules they set for agricultural trade
Summarize non-tariff trade barriers, such as sanitary and phytosanitary standards, labeling rules, and biosecurity requirements, that affect agricultural imports and exports
Analyze how differing national regulations on genetically engineered crops affect international trade and public acceptance of United States agricultural products
Analyze the effects of a government farm program, such as crop insurance subsidies or price supports, on farmer decision-making
Analyze how exchange rates and global macroeconomic trends affect the competitiveness of United States agricultural exports
Evaluate the impact of a trade policy change, such as a tariff or embargo, on United States agricultural exports
Predict future export trends for a specific agricultural commodity based on current trade agreements, policy conditions, and global markets
Recommend how an agribusiness or SAE enterprise could adapt to a change in global trade conditions or trade policy
Justify a position on an agricultural policy issue using economic evidence and reasoning, such as in an FFA Agricultural Issues Forum presentation

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, rewording the grade 12 one to tie it to the FFA Agricultural Issues Forum. Added objectives on imported foods and why they are grown abroad, major trading partners, comparative advantage, the purpose of the Farm Bill, trade and food security, the role of exports in the economy, how agricultural policy is made, trade agreements and institutions, non-tariff barriers, biotechnology regulation in trade, exchange rates, export trend prediction, and adapting an agribusiness or SAE to trade changes. Price formation and commodity trading are left to the sibling sub-topics. Attached AFNR standards only to objectives at grade 9 and above where the standard is directly taught.
